BASE_AUTHORITY.byte_unchanged: MANDATORY AND VERIFIED. This errata does not edit v1.0.0. It supersedes named clauses by appending, exactly as the Quiesce amendment v1.0.1 did to its own parent.

CERTIFICATION_CONSUMED.subject: STAGING_QUIESCE_READONLY_CENSUS_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json and its companion manifest (PR #209 head 0b69ea10382660a934737325afc3a1291447482a).
CERTIFICATION_CONSUMED.disposition: The failure is narrow and mechanical: one count defect (B-C1) and ten narrower-but-real corrections (NBF-1..NBF-11, NBF-5 not issued). None reopens SECTION_G's central conclusion that C3_AVAILABLE is unreachable under this authority; several corrections (NBF-8 in particular) make C3_NOT_AVAILABLE the even more clearly expected outcome. This errata closes every directive in the brief that reached this lane and defers nothing it could close.
CERTIFICATION_CONSUMED.self_criticism_recorded_once: B-C1 is the certifier's cleanest catch: a hand-counted arithmetic string ('Fifteen observations: five plus nine plus two') that does not equal 5+9+2=16, propagated unchecked into eight downstream loci because each one trusted the label rather than re-deriving it. The corrected count_check is a structural array whose length a script can check, precisely so this class of defect cannot recur silently.

SECTION_B1_OBSERVATION_COUNT_CORRECTION.the_defect: SECTION_E_AUTHORIZED_READ_SET of v1.0.0 lists OBS-V0 through OBS-V4 (five Vercel entries), OBS-S1 through OBS-S9 (nine Supabase entries) and OBS-L1/OBS-L2 (two local entries) -- 5 + 9 + 2 = SIXTEEN -- while count_check, SECTION_H's per-observation and package-level evidence-contract fields, HCC-1's act/prestate_shown/verification, self_check.checks[7] and next_gate all assert FIFTEEN. The arithmetic was never re-derived from the actual array lengths; it was carried as a label.

the_certifier_established_about_OBS_V4.no_consuming_decision_rule: No rule in SECTION_G reads OBS-V4's result. v1.0.0 says so itself at OBS-V4.HARD_LIMITS[3]: 'This observation may be SKIPPED entirely. Its result is not an input to any rule in SECTION_G.'
the_certifier_established_about_OBS_V4.no_named_target: OBS-V4's method is 'a deployment's public health surface' with no deployment identified -- it has no target until OBS-V3 has already run, and even then no rule consumes what it would return.
the_certifier_established_about_OBS_V4.no_bounded_quantity: It records only 'the HTTP status code and whether the response was served by the platform's access-protection layer', neither of which is compared against a threshold or fed into a formula anywhere in this pair.
the_certifier_established_about_OBS_V4.explicitly_optional: v1.0.0 states it is 'OPTIONAL AND STRICTLY BOUNDED' and 'may be SKIPPED entirely'.

the_correction.rule: SUPERSEDE OBS-V4 IN FULL: NOT_AUTHORIZED, REMOVED_FROM_EFFECTIVE_READ_SET. It is not narrowed, retimed or re-scoped -- it is withdrawn, because an observation with no consuming rule, no bound and an explicit skip clause is exactly the kind of item that should never have been counted as part of the authorized ceiling, and CF-2's own finding (the liveness half of P-10's evidence contract cannot be performed read-only in any useful form) removes its last reason to exist.
the_correction.U1_5_disposition: U1-5 (whether a live deployment can be asked non-destructively which database identity it holds) reverts to NOT CLOSED BY ANY OBSERVATION IN THIS PAIR. This is not a new gap: v1.0.0 already answered U1-5 negatively in substance ('IT CANNOT, WITHOUT CAUSING A WRITE') and OBS-V4 was a liveness-only consolation prize that fed no rule. Removing it removes a null operation, not evidence.
the_correction.no_reduction_of_MGQ1_coverage: MG-Q1's own closure definition (PMV-1) never required a liveness probe. U1-1 through U1-4 are closed exactly as before by OBS-V0 through OBS-V3, unaffected by this correction.

EFFECTIVE_READ_SET_v1_0_1.rule: Proved by ENUMERATION, not by a hand-written arithmetic string. The array below IS the effective read set; its length IS the count, and a certifier or a script can check len(effective_observation_ids) without parsing prose.
EFFECTIVE_READ_SET_v1_0_1.count_is_len_of_effective_observation_id: MECHANICALLY TRUE: len(effective_observation_ids) == 15 by direct count of the array above, re-derivable by any JSON parser without arithmetic on a prose string.

SECTION_B4_OBS_S2_SERVICES_PARAMETER.the_defect: GET /v1/projects/{ref}/health carries a REQUIRED query parameter, services, which v1.0.0's OBS-S2 never names. Without it the request is malformed and the observation is not executable as written.

measured_parameter_contract.source: Re-derived from the same pinned specification, sha256 5b11a7fd32ed31bac59170c02e14f1619d0f0218a78b7fab3be41d3f2d69b600, GET /v1/projects/{ref}/health.parameters.
measured_parameter_contract.services: required=true, in=query, a comma-separated list or array of enum values: auth, db, db_postgres_user, pooler, realtime, rest, storage, pg_bouncer.

the_minimum_set_derived_not_assumed.rule: Derived strictly from which services SECTION_G's rules actually consume, per the brief's instruction not to request unrelated services.
the_minimum_set_derived_not_assumed.G-N3_needs: auth -- 'OBS-S2 reports the Auth service present and healthy'.
the_minimum_set_derived_not_assumed.G-N4_needs: rest -- 'OBS-S2 reports the Data API service healthy'; Data API is PostgREST, whose service-health enum value is rest.
the_minimum_set_derived_not_assumed.not_requested_and_why: db, db_postgres_user, pooler, pg_bouncer are not read by any G-N or G-U rule and are not requested. realtime is likewise not consumed by any G-N rule (OBS-S6's config/realtime GET, not /health, is what U2-1 uses for Realtime, and it is CONFIGURATION only per its own explicit_limit) -- so realtime is also not requested from /health.

healthy_vs_status.measured: The V1ServiceHealthResponse_Output schema marks the healthy boolean field 'deprecated: true, description: Deprecated. Use status instead', and defines status as an enum COMING_UP | ACTIVE_HEALTHY | UNHEALTHY. Both fields are in the schema's required list, so healthy is still returned, but the vendor names status as its replacement.
healthy_vs_status.the_correction: OBS-S2 records status as the primary field for every G-N rule's condition ('reports ... healthy' is re-read as 'reports status == ACTIVE_HEALTHY'), and records healthy alongside it as a cross-check, never as the sole basis for a G-N trigger going forward.
healthy_vs_status.no_change_to_the_rules_semantics: This is a field-preference correction, not a logic change: a service that is ACTIVE_HEALTHY is healthy under either field in every case this chain has measured, and the correction exists so a future API version that removes the deprecated field does not silently break G-N3/G-N4/G-N5.

Use this if you're building a third-party app that needs to create or manage Supabase projects on behalf of your users. SECTION_B6_TEAM_LEVEL_ENV_SCOPE.the_gap: PR #201's own PMV-2 states in terms that it 'did NOT verify' whether the branch-override rule holds against a TEAM-level shared variable as opposed to a PROJECT-level row, and that if PMV-2 finds a team-level shared variable 'the override mechanism is UNPROVEN for this case.' v1.0.0's U1-2 and OBS-V2 do not account for this distinction at all: TARGET SCOPE is named as one of the four permitted fields but is never defined precisely enough to say whether it captures team-level-vs-project-level.

the_correction.TARGET_SCOPE_definition_extended: TARGET SCOPE, as recorded by OBS-V2, is defined to include whether a row is a PROJECT-level row (targeting one or more of Production/Preview/Development on the enumerated project) or a TEAM-level SHARED variable attached to that project, wherever the tool surface used (vercel env list, or the equivalent API read) exposes that distinction. This is a SCOPE fact, not a value, and sits squarely inside the field PMV-1 already permits -- no fifth field is added.
the_correction.fail_closed_when_undeterminable: Where the tool surface does NOT expose a team-vs-project indicator for a given row within the four permitted fields, that row's scope classification is recorded as UNKNOWN with reason TEAM_LEVEL_SCOPE_UNDETERMINED. It is NOT assumed to be project-level, and it is NOT assumed to be team-level.
the_correction.consequence_for_SECTION_G: A PRESENT row whose team-vs-project classification is UNKNOWN is treated identically to any other PRESENT row under G-N2 (if a READY deployment applies) or G-U2 (if none does) -- the existing rules already fail closed on an unmeasured target per U1-3's structural limit, and this correction does not weaken or bypass that. It adds precision to what TARGET SCOPE means; it does not add a new decision path.

new_measurement_gap_recorded.gap: Whether vercel env list (or its API equivalent) surfaces a team-level shared variable identically to a project-level row, or requires a separate team-scoped read to be seen at all by OBS-V2's per-project enumeration method, is UNMEASURED by this lane.
new_measurement_gap_recorded.consequence: If a team-level shared row exists but is NOT surfaced by a per-project env-list call, OBS-V2 could under-enumerate U1-2 without any observation reporting a failure -- a silent gap rather than a G-U3 OBSERVATION_INCOMPLETE.
new_measurement_gap_recorded.closure: The execution lane's first act under OBS-V2 must check, from the actual tool output it is using, whether a team/shared-scope listing surface exists and is distinct from the per-project surface; if so, both are read. This is recorded as a method requirement on OBS-V2, not resolved here.

SECTION_B7_GN3_TOKEN_REFRESH_CORRECTION.the_defect: v1.0.0's G-N3 condition is a CONJUNCTION: 'OBS-S2 reports the Auth service present and healthy, AND OBS-S3 reports any sign-in path enabled'. Its own ground text already states the true reach correctly -- 'a stale browser tab performing a TOKEN REFRESH' -- but the condition does not test for token-refresh reach at all. Sign-in flags (disable_signup, external_*_enabled, external_anonymous_users_enabled) govern whether a NEW client can authenticate. They do NOT govern whether an ALREADY-ISSUED session can refresh its token, because GoTrue's refresh-token grant is a property of the token, not of the signup/signin configuration.
SECTION_B7_GN3_TOKEN_REFRESH_CORRECTION.why_this_is_a_false_negative_risk: Under the conjunctive form, a project with Auth healthy but every sign-in path disabled (disable_signup=true, no external providers, anonymous disabled) would NOT trigger G-N3, even though any session issued before those flags were set -- or any session issued through a channel the flags do not gate -- can still reach GoTrue via token refresh and write auth.sessions / auth.refresh_tokens. A Tier-1-only census could therefore reach a run where G-N3 stays silent while a real client-write surface remains open, which is precisely the false 'empty-by-construction' signal the brief instructs this correction to prevent.

the_correction.condition_v1_0_1: OBS-S2 reports the Auth service present with status ACTIVE_HEALTHY (healthy=true as a cross-check per SECTION_B4's field preference).
the_correction.ground_v1_0_1: A reachable, healthy GoTrue is a client surface for token refresh REGARDLESS of sign-up/sign-in configuration: the parent's own W-4 measurement states in terms that 'a previously issued session' or 'a stale browser tab performing a token refresh' reaches GoTrue directly and writes auth.sessions and auth.refresh_tokens, and nothing in disable_signup or the external-provider flags disables the refresh-token grant for a session issued before, or through a channel outside, those flags. Sign-in-path exposure (OBS-S3) governs whether NEW clients can authenticate; it does not govern whether EXISTING sessions can write, so it is dropped from the trigger condition and is no longer a required conjunct.
the_correction.OBS_S3_retained_as_diagnostic: OBS-S3 remains authorized and still closes U2-1 for W-4's hosted_exposure_at_the_governed_ref sub-key -- its disable_signup and external-provider fields remain useful DIAGNOSTIC context for the re-adjudication brief (whether NEW clients could ALSO reach it) -- but its result no longer gates G-N3's firing.
the_correction.consequence: G-N3 now fires whenever Auth is reachable and healthy, independent of sign-in configuration. This makes C3_NOT_AVAILABLE the practically-certain Tier-1 outcome for any live, healthy Supabase project, which this errata records as the HONEST consequence of the measured token-refresh reach rather than as an overreach: the parent authority already established that no act in this chain can make GoTrue non-writing, and a trigger that failed to fire whenever Auth was merely configured cautiously would have understated that finding.

OF_C3_corrected.the_prior_framing: v1.0.0's OF-C3 described G-N3 as 'deliberately broader than the amendment's illustrative phrase' by dropping the live-session count while KEEPING the sign-in-flag conjunct.
OF_C3_corrected.the_corrected_framing: G-N3 is now broader still: it drops the sign-in-flag conjunct as well, because that conjunct tested new-client reach, not the token-refresh reach that is the actual W-4 hazard. The open question for a certifier is no longer 'is dropping the live-session count faithful to the amendment's phrase' alone, but whether ANY exposure test short of a Tier 2 session census can ever be faithful to 'before any client of any kind exists' -- and this errata's position, stated plainly, is that it cannot, which is exactly why A-4 (Tier 2) remains the only route to C3_AVAILABLE and G-N3 alone cannot manufacture a false negative on that question any more.
